1: Once, when thought came to me of the things that are, and my mind soared high, and my senses were stilled as in a heavy sleep, there came before me a being of vast magnitude, who called me by name and said: What wouldst thou hear and see, and what wouldst thou learn and know?

And I saw in my mind a great light, and in the light a shape whose face was the face of a man. And the shape said: I am Poimandres, the mind of sovereignty. And I said: Thou art the word by which all things were made, and the maker is mind, and the word and the mind are one.
[Poimandres 12 — The fall of the light into matter]

The word leapt down upon the water, and the water was stirred, and smoke and mist rose from it, and there was a voice like the voice of fire. And mind, the father of all, brought forth the word; and the word, going forth upon the elements, fashioned the world.
2: The maker of all, the mind, filled a great bowl with mind, and sent it down to men, and appointed a herald to them, saying: Plunge into the bowl, every soul that can; for I mixed the bowl for the soul that would be washed.
[Corpus Hermeticum IV 4 — The baptism of mind]

They that plunged into the bowl, they were made partakers of mind, and they that had mind received the knowledge, and they were made whole. But they that would not plunge walked on in the way of the body, and they forgot the bowl and what it was for.
[Corpus Hermeticum V 2 — The gratitude of the seen world]

Look at the order of the world, and give thanks to its maker; for the world is the son of God, and man is the son of the world, and all things are bound in the chain of gratitude, and gratitude is the beginning of knowledge.
3: The soul that knows itself takes wings, and soars above the body, and looks down upon the body as upon a garment that is laid aside. And knowing itself immortal, it is afraid no more, and it is free.
[Corpus Hermeticum XI 20 — The measure of God]

God is not measured by time, nor contained in place, nor bounded by anything that is made. All things are in God, as the fruit is in the seed, and the seed is in the tree, and the tree is in the ground, and the ground is in the world, and the world is in God.
[Corpus Hermeticum XIII 22 — The song of the reborn]

From eternity I give thanks to God the Father of all. Thy word, O Lord, is the hymn of all Thy works; and Thy wisdom is the singer of Thy hymn. Accept, O Life and Light, the offering of a soul that has seen Thee — for by Thee was I made, and in Thee am I reborn.
